# Formula sheet {#sec-formulas}

All formulas of the block on one page, collected session by session. Use it to revise, and as a model for your own handwritten cheat sheet. Your own sheet will be more useful if you write it yourself and add the mistakes you tend to make.

## Session 1: Numbers

| Topic | Formula |
|---------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| Fractions | $\dfrac{a}{b} + \dfrac{c}{d} = \dfrac{ad + bc}{bd}$, $\quad \dfrac{a}{b} \cdot \dfrac{c}{d} = \dfrac{ac}{bd}$, $\quad \dfrac{a}{b} : \dfrac{c}{d} = \dfrac{a}{b} \cdot \dfrac{d}{c}$ |
| Percent | part $=$ rate $\cdot$ base |
| Growth factor | new $=$ old $\cdot (1 + p)$; several changes: multiply the factors |
| VAT | gross $=$ net $\cdot (1 + \text{VAT rate})$, $\quad$ net $= \dfrac{\text{gross}}{1 + \text{VAT rate}}$ |
| Markup, margin | markup $= \dfrac{\text{price} - \text{cost}}{\text{cost}}$, $\quad$ margin $= \dfrac{\text{price} - \text{cost}}{\text{price}}$ |
| Percent change | $\dfrac{\text{new} - \text{old}}{\text{old}}$ |
| Powers | $a^m a^n = a^{m+n}$, $\ \dfrac{a^m}{a^n} = a^{m-n}$, $\ (a^m)^n = a^{mn}$, $\ a^0 = 1$, $\ a^{-n} = \dfrac{1}{a^n}$, $\ a^{1/n} = \sqrt[n]{a}$ |
| Average growth rate | $p = \left(\dfrac{\text{end}}{\text{start}}\right)^{1/n} - 1$ |
| Binomial formulas | $(a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2$, $\ (a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2$, $\ (a + b)(a - b) = a^2 - b^2$ |

## Session 2: Equations

| Topic | Formula |
|---------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| Cost, revenue, profit | $C = F + v\,q$, $\quad R = p\,q$, $\quad P = R - C = (p - v)\,q - F$ |
| Contribution margin | $p - v$ |
| Break-even volume | $q = \dfrac{F}{p - v}$ |
| Volume for a target profit $P$ | $q = \dfrac{P + F}{p - v}$ |
| Quadratic formula | $a x^2 + b x + c = 0 \ \Rightarrow\ x_{1,2} = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$ |
| *pq*-formula | $x^2 + p x + q = 0 \ \Rightarrow\ x_{1,2} = -\dfrac{p}{2} \pm \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{p}{2}\right)^2 - q}$ |
| Discriminant | $D = b^2 - 4ac$: two solutions if $D > 0$, one if $D = 0$, none if $D < 0$ |

## Session 3: Functions

| Topic | Formula |
|---------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| Linear function | $f(x) = m x + b$ (slope $m$, intercept $b$) |
| Slope from two points | $m = \dfrac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}$, $\quad b = y_1 - m x_1$ |
| Average cost | $AC(q) = \dfrac{C(q)}{q} = \dfrac{F}{q} + v$ |
| Market equilibrium | Demand price $=$ supply price |
| Vertex of a parabola | $f(x) = a x^2 + b x + c$: $\ x_{\text{vertex}} = -\dfrac{b}{2a}$ (maximum if $a < 0$, minimum if $a > 0$) |
| Exponential function | $f(t) = a\,(1 + p)^t$ |
| Logarithm | $\log_b(x) = y \iff b^y = x$; $\ \ln(a b) = \ln a + \ln b$, $\ \ln\!\left(\frac{a}{b}\right) = \ln a - \ln b$, $\ \ln(a^t) = t \ln a$ |
| Time to reach a target | $n = \dfrac{\ln(K_n / K_0)}{\ln(1 + i)}$ |
| Rule of 70 | Doubling time $\approx \dfrac{70}{\text{rate in percent}}$ |

## Session 4: Money over time

| Topic | Formula |
|---------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| Simple interest | $K_n = K_0 \,(1 + i\,n)$ |
| Compound interest | $K_n = K_0 \, q^n$ with $q = 1 + i$ |
| Interest $m$ times a year | $K_n = K_0 \left(1 + \dfrac{i}{m}\right)^{m n}$ |
| Effective annual rate | $i_{\text{eff}} = \left(1 + \dfrac{i}{m}\right)^m - 1$ |
| Skonto as a yearly rate | $\dfrac{\text{discount}}{100 - \text{discount}} \cdot \dfrac{365}{\text{days gained}}$ |
| Present value | $K_0 = \dfrac{K_n}{q^n}$ |
| Net present value | $NPV = -I_0 + \dfrac{C_1}{q} + \dfrac{C_2}{q^2} + \dots + \dfrac{C_n}{q^n}$; invest if $NPV > 0$ |
| Geometric series | $1 + q + \dots + q^{n-1} = \dfrac{q^n - 1}{q - 1}$ |
| Savings plan (final value) | $R_n = R \cdot \dfrac{q^n - 1}{q - 1}$ |
| Regular payments (present value) | $R_0 = R \cdot \dfrac{1 - q^{-n}}{i}$ |
| Loan instalment | $A = K_0 \cdot \dfrac{i \, q^n}{q^n - 1}$ |
| Remaining debt after $k$ periods | $K_k = K_0 \, q^k - A \cdot \dfrac{q^k - 1}{q - 1}$ |
| Straight-line depreciation | $D = \dfrac{A_0 - R}{n}$, $\quad B_t = A_0 - D\,t$ |
| Declining-balance depreciation | $B_t = A_0 \,(1 - p)^t$ |
